## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `hui-media-player-playback-card-feature`

**What changed:** The component-level `static styles` block previously included an additional `css` block alongside `cardFeatureStyles`:

```js
// BEFORE (removed in this diff)
static styles = [
  cardFeatureStyles,
  css`
    ha-control-button-group {
      overflow: hidden;
    }
  `,
];

// AFTER
static styles = cardFeatureStyles;
```

The `overflow: hidden` rule on the internal `ha-control-button-group` element inside the media player playback card feature has been removed. This was the fix for a clipped focus ring — the overflow clipping was intentionally removed to allow focus rings to render fully.

**Effect on ha-lcars:** ha-lcars does not explicitly target `hui-media-player-playback-card-feature` or `ha-control-button-group` in any of its `card-mod-card-yaml`, `card-mod-row-yaml`, or other injected CSS blocks. However, removing `overflow: hidden` from the component's internal shadow DOM means the playback button group may now visually overflow its container. On LCARS-styled cards (which use `overflow: hidden` and precise border-radius geometry on button containers), this could result in focus rings or button elements extending beyond card frame boundaries that ha-lcars defines via rules like:

```css
/* In card-mod-card-yaml, button shape classes */
> ha-card, > #aspect-ratio > ha-card, &:is(ha-card) {
  border-radius: 0px;
  ...
}
```

**Suggested fix:** Monitor whether the media player card feature's playback buttons visually overflow LCARS card frames. If so, add a targeted card-mod rule:

```yaml
"hui-media-player-playback-card-feature $": |
  ha-control-button-group {
    overflow: hidden;
  }
```

This re-applies the removed clipping at the theme level without depending on the component's own styles.

### Component: `hui-entity-card` / `hui-statistic-card` (sensor graph footer)

**What changed:** Both `hui-entity-card` and `hui-statistic-card` now add a `ll-upgrade` event listener on lazy-loaded footer elements (e.g., `hui-graph-header-footer`) to forward `hass` after the element upgrades. Previously, the `hass` property was not forwarded to lazy footers until the next full render cycle.

**Effect on ha-lcars:** ha-lcars's `card-mod-card-yaml` injection targets the card host (`:host`) and immediate children via selectors like `> :not(style,card-mod,h1)`. Footer elements such as `hui-graph-header-footer` are children of the card's shadow DOM and receive inherited CSS custom properties. The timing fix means graph footer elements now receive `hass` (and thus render/animate) sooner after lazy loading.

The visual consequence is that graph footers — including any bar chart or sparkline rendered by `hui-graph-header-footer` — will now paint during the same render cycle as the card, rather than on a deferred update. This means the `--primary-background-color: var(--lcars-dark-gray)` override applied via:

```yaml
"ha-card ha-gauge$": |
  .gauge {
    --primary-background-color: var(--lcars-dark-gray);
  }
```

…and similar footer-targeted variable injection will now take effect at first paint rather than on a subsequent update. This is net-positive for theme consistency, but theme authors should verify that graph footer colors (history graph fills, which consume `lcars-ui-accent-color: var(--lcars-orange)`) render correctly on first display rather than flashing unstyled briefly.

**Suggested fix:** No CSS change needed. Verify visually that `hui-graph-header-footer` sparklines render with correct LCARS colors (`--lcars-ui-accent-color`, `--primary-background-color: var(--lcars-dark-gray)`) on initial card load. No fix required unless a flash of unstyled content is observed, in which case ensuring `--primary-background-color` is set at the `:host` level of the card (already done in `card-mod-card-yaml`) is sufficient.

## LOW IMPACT

### Component: `hass-router-page` (panel routing)

**What changed:** A new private field `_replacingPanel` is introduced on `HassRouterPage` to suppress property forwarding to outgoing panels during route transitions. This prevents incoming panel properties from being forwarded while a loading screen or outgoing panel is still visible.

**Effect on ha-lcars:** This is a pure logic change. ha-lcars does not target `hass-router-page` directly, nor does it inject CSS into its shadow DOM. There is no CSS custom property, element selector, or layout token involved.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed. This change may slightly improve the visual consistency of panel transitions (no stale property state on outgoing panels), which is theme-neutral.

---

### Component: `hui-graph-header-footer` (history subscription guard)

**What changed:** The `_subscribeHistory()` guard condition was reordered to check `this.hass` and `this._config` for nullishness before calling `isComponentLoaded(this.hass.config, "history")`. This prevents a null-dereference on `this.hass` when the subscription fires before `hass` is set.

**Effect on ha-lcars:** Pure defensive logic change with no CSS, variable, or DOM structure impact. Graph footer elements targeted by theme CSS (via inherited custom properties from card hosts) are unaffected structurally.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed. Informational only.
